vendor_message_text: Failed to read linecard [dec] muxbuffer supervisor selection register
vendor_explanation: The active supervisor tried to read alignment information for the switching module slot's mux buffer from the chassis mux buffer module, but was unable to do so. This information is needed to make sure that switching module slot's mux buffer is aligned towards the active supervisor engine.
vendor_recommended_action: If this message appears only once for a switching module, this could be a transient error and no action is required. If this message appears repeatedly (once every 5 minutes) on one or more switching modules please contact your technical support representative to replace the supervisor engine and chassis.

vendor_message_text: Failed to read mux buffer [dec]'s serial eeprom
vendor_explanation: Reading the mux buffer serial eeprom failed.
vendor_recommended_action: Copy the error message exactly as it appears on the console or in the system log. Research and attempt to resolve the error using the Output Interpreter https://www.cisco.com/cgi-bin/Support/OutputInterpreter/home.pl. Issue the show tech-support command to gather data that may help identify the nature of the error. Also perform a search of the Bug Toolkit http://www.cisco.com/cgi-bin/Support/Bugtool/home.pl. If you still require assistance, open a case with the Technical Assistance Center via the Internet http://tools.cisco.com/ServiceRequestTool/create/launch.do, or contact your Cisco technical support.

vendor_message_text: Linecard mux buffers may mis-align to incorrect supervisor due to mux buffer reset with other supervisor desires to be active
vendor_explanation: While putting switching module mux-buffers in reset and taking them out of reset, other supervisor engine is trying to become active using hardware hot-standby logic. This may cause incorrect alignment of switching module slot's mux buffer towards the non-active supervisor engine causing complete datapath failure.
vendor_recommended_action: If this happens, please contact Cisco Technical Support representative to report the failure and reset the other supervisor using the redundancy reload peer command to fix this condition.

vendor_message_text: Netflow Services Card seeprom read failed
vendor_explanation: Reading the Netflow Services Card serial eeprom failed.
vendor_recommended_action: Copy the error message exactly as it appears on the console or in the system log. Research and attempt to resolve the error using the Output Interpreter https://www.cisco.com/cgi-bin/Support/OutputInterpreter/home.pl. Issue the show tech-support command to gather data that may help identify the nature of the error. Also perform a search of the Bug Toolkit http://www.cisco.com/cgi-bin/Support/Bugtool/home.pl. If you still require assistance, open a case with the Technical Assistance Center via the Internet http://tools.cisco.com/ServiceRequestTool/create/launch.do, or contact your Cisco technical support.

vendor_message_text: WS-X4124-FX-MT revision [dec].[dec], which is < 1.6, is not supported
vendor_explanation: WS-X4124-FX-MT modules with revisions < 1.6 are not supported.
vendor_recommended_action: This module needs to be replaced with a WS-X4124-FX-MT module that has a newer hardware revision number.

vendor_message_text: Port [char] has a non-LX SFP, which is not supported
vendor_explanation: The WS-X4448-GB-LX module supports only LX SFPs. It marks any other type of Small Form-Factor Pluggable (SFP) as faulty.
vendor_recommended_action: Replace the SFP with an LX SFP that Cisco supports.

vendor_message_text: Ran out of memory - cannot allocate internal buffers
vendor_explanation: The switch ran out of memory in the temporary buffers.
vendor_recommended_action: If this message reappears, reboot the switch.

vendor_message_text: Failed to communicate with power supply in slot [dec].
vendor_explanation: A Read/Write command issued to the power supply failed.
vendor_recommended_action: Reinsert the power supply. If the error recurs, hotswap it with a new power supply.

vendor_message_text: Invalid data in power supply [dec]'s serial eeprom
vendor_explanation: The power supply serial EEPROM could not be read or has not been programmed.
vendor_recommended_action: This message may appear twice. Enter the show idprom power-supply {number} and the show power commands. If the power-supply idprom information and status display successfully, disregard the message. Otherwise, remove and re-insert the power supply. If the problem persists, hotswap it with a new power supply.

vendor_message_text: Failed to read power supply [dec]'s serial eeprom
vendor_explanation: Reading the power supply serial EEPROM failed.
vendor_recommended_action: This message may appear twice. Enter the show idprom power-supply {number} and the show power commands. If the power-supply idprom information and status display successfully, disregard the message. Otherwise, remove and re-insert the power supply. If the problem persists, hotswap it with a new power supply.

vendor_message_text: Failed to read power supply [dec]'s status register
vendor_explanation: Reading the power supply status register failed.
vendor_recommended_action: Re-insert the power supply. If that doesn't work, hotswap it with a new power supply.

vendor_message_text: Error reading back module [dec]s serial EEPROM data after write
vendor_explanation: After writing a module's serial EEPROM in response to a CLI request, the switch tried to read it back in, to ensure that the correct values were written out. What the switch read back in differs from what the switch wrote out. The read or write might fail if the module is not seated correctly in the slot.
vendor_recommended_action: Remove and reinsert the module. If that does not work, reboot the switch. If the problem persists, contact your technical support representative. You will likely have to return the module to Cisco to reprogram or replace the serial EEPROM.

vendor_message_text: Stub type mismatch: stub [dec]/[dec] is type [dec], should be type [dec]
vendor_explanation: The stubs have non-matching physical types for the specified module.
vendor_recommended_action: Verify that the physical types for every stub on the module match.

vendor_message_text: The idprom of the currently installed fan tray does not contain valid data.
vendor_explanation: The fantray is operating properly, but could not be identified. For some supervisor engine, chassis, and fan tray combinations the power consumption allocated to the fan tray may be higher than the fan tray is actually consuming.
vendor_recommended_action: Replace the fan tray.

vendor_message_text: A fan tray, among the currently installed fantrays, is not functioning.
vendor_explanation: There are enough fantrays in the system, but some have failed.
vendor_recommended_action: Replace the fan tray.

vendor_message_text: All fantrays are in good working condition, system has recovered from a partial fantray failure.
vendor_explanation: There are enough fan trays in the system and all are operational. Some failed fan trays were removed or replaced.
vendor_recommended_action: No action is required.

vendor_message_text: Failed to identify the Supervisor in Slot [dec]'s
vendor_explanation: SW can not recognize this supervisor. This supervisor is either unsupported or faulty.
vendor_recommended_action: Try removing and reinserting the module. If that doesn't work, try resetting the switch. If the read still fails, this module needs to be returned.

vendor_message_text: Supervisor's FPGA register type is [dec], but supervisor's serial eeprom type is [dec]
vendor_explanation: The type in the supervisor engine's FPGA register doesn't match the type in the supervisor engine's serial EEPROM. This might happen if the IDPROM is misprogrammed or the supervisor engine's FPGA register somehow returns an incorrect value. Both are extremely unlikely.
vendor_recommended_action: Check the FruMinorType field in the supervisor engine's serial EEPROM, using the show idprom supervisor command. The output should be the same as the number printed in this log message for the FPGA register type. This should never happen with a production supervisor engine. If it does, replace the supervisor engine.

vendor_message_text: Transceiver integrity check on port [char] failed
vendor_explanation: Non-Cisco-qualified transceivers are permitted but may give unpredictable results.
vendor_recommended_action: Copy the error message exactly as it appears on the console or in the system log. Research and attempt to resolve the error using the Output Interpreter https://www.cisco.com/cgi-bin/Support/OutputInterpreter/home.pl. Issue the show tech-support command to gather data that may help identify the nature of the error. Also perform a search of the Bug Toolkit http://www.cisco.com/cgi-bin/Support/Bugtool/home.pl. If you still require assistance, open a case with the Technical Assistance Center via the Internet http://tools.cisco.com/ServiceRequestTool/create/launch.do, or contact your Cisco technical support.

vendor_message_text: transceiver integrity check on port [char] failed: bad crc
vendor_explanation: The checksum of the transceiver SEEPROM is not valid, indicating a bad or non-Cisco transceiver. Only Cisco-qualified transceivers are supported. Other transceivers will cause the associated port to show as faulty.
vendor_recommended_action: Replace the transceiver with a transceiver that Cisco supports.

vendor_message_text: transceiver integrity check on port [char] failed: bad key
vendor_explanation: Only Cisco-qualified transceivers are supported. Other transceivers will cause the associated port to show as faulty.
vendor_recommended_action: Replace the transceiver with an transceiver that Cisco supports.

vendor_message_text: transceivers on ports [char] and [char] have duplicate serial numbers
vendor_explanation: Only Cisco-qualified transceivers are supported. Other transceivers place the associated port in the faulty status.All transceivers must have a unique serial number. If this message appears you likely have a cloned transceiver SEEPROM.
vendor_recommended_action: Replace the transceiver with a transceiver that Cisco supports.

vendor_message_text: Unknown module (Field Replaceable Unit minor type [dec]) in slot [dec]
vendor_explanation: The module's serial EEPROM was readable, and your software image does not recognize this module. A software upgrade is necessary.
vendor_recommended_action: Upgrade the software to a version that is compatible with the module.

vendor_message_text: Writing the supervisor's SPROM is not supported
vendor_explanation: Rewriting the supervisor engine's serial programmable read-only memory (SPROM) is not allowed, because if it is done incorrectly, it could make the system unusable.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Resuming normal phone operation since inline power has been restored
vendor_explanation: PoE to the switch was restored, and normal phone operation will resume.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: GalChassisVp: Linecard in Slot [dec] failed to boot on STANDBY Supervisor
vendor_explanation: Inserted linecard failed to boot on STANDBY supervisor.Explanation    No action is required.Error Message    C4K_CHASSIS-4-OVERHEATINGOVER: Resuming normal operation after return to acceptable temperatures.Explanation    The unit's modules were reset to reduce heat generation, because the unit reached a critical temperature. The switch is now cool enough to return to normal operation.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Other supervisor is still holding hardware lock
vendor_explanation: This condition is detected when redundancy register indicates that other supervisor is holding lock when it is not due to hardware signal latency. Unless there is a real hardware failure, the system recovers from this state. If there is a persistent hardware failure this message will be seen four times.
vendor_recommended_action: Copy the error message exactly as it appears on the console or in the system log. Research and attempt to resolve the error using the Output Interpreter https://www.cisco.com/cgi-bin/Support/OutputInterpreter/home.pl. Issue the show tech-support command to gather data that may help identify the nature of the error. Also perform a search of the Bug Toolkit http://www.cisco.com/cgi-bin/Support/Bugtool/home.pl. If you still require assistance, open a case with the Technical Assistance Center via the Internet http://tools.cisco.com/ServiceRequestTool/create/launch.do, or contact your Cisco technical support.

vendor_message_text: The power supply in slot [dec] has experienced a power failure.
vendor_explanation: One of the installed power supplies has experienced a power failure.
vendor_recommended_action: Power cycle the power supply. If the problem reoccurs, replace the power supply.

vendor_message_text: Power supply in slot [dec] is not supported on this  platform.Recommended Action    An unsupported power supply has been detected. This power supply was not designed for this platform and should be replaced.Recommended Action    Replace power supply with a supported supply type.Error Message    C4K_CHASSIS-4-SLOTOVERHEATINGOVER: Resuming normal operation in slot [dec] after return to acceptable temperatures.
vendor_explanation: The module has been reset to reduce heat generation since it exceeded critical temperature. It has returned to acceptable temperature and normal operation is resuming.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Some temperature sensors on module [dec] have failed
vendor_explanation: Some temperature sensors on the module have failed. This may restrict the module's ability to detect over-temperature conditions. If further sensors fail, the module will be unable to detect over-temperature conditions.
vendor_recommended_action: If this message appears only once, this could be a transient error and no action is required. If this message appears repeatedly (such as, once every hour), return the module for repair.

vendor_message_text: Spurious fantray removal detected
vendor_explanation: Spurious fantray removals were detected.
vendor_recommended_action: If this message appears only once, this could be a transient error and no action is required. If this message occurs repeatedly(such as, once every hour), have the fantray repaired.

vendor_message_text: Resuming normal operation after restoration of adequate fan cooling
vendor_explanation: The modules were reset to reduce heat generation because there were not enough working fans. Adequate fan cooling is now restored, and the switch will resume normal operation.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Module in slot [dec] resuming normal operation after restoration of adequate power
vendor_explanation: The module was reset to conserve power because the system had inadequate power available. The switch now has adequate power and is resuming normal operation.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Resuming normal operation after restoration of adequate power
vendor_explanation: The switch reset the modules to conserve power, but it now has adequate power and will resume normal operation.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: TDR test is in progress on interface [char]
vendor_explanation: The TDR test is already in progress on this interface.
vendor_recommended_action: Try the command again after the test is completed.

vendor_message_text: [char] is not supported on this interface
vendor_explanation: The online diagnostic test requested cannot be run on the specified port.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: [char] is not supported on this port
vendor_explanation: The online diagnostic test requested cannot be run on the specified port.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: [char] is not supported on port connector type: [char]
vendor_explanation: This online diagnostic test cannot be run on the specified port with the current connector type. If the connector type changes to copper, it may be possible to run the test.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Unsupported transceiver found in [char]
vendor_explanation: The transceiver was identified as an unsupported non-Cisco transceiver.
vendor_recommended_action: If this transceiver was purchased from Cisco, contact Cisco TAC to get the transceiver replaced.

vendor_message_text: Poe fixed on slot [dec] (count=[dec])
vendor_explanation: Under very rare conditions, due to an anomaly in hardware state that includes transients in input power supply, PoE on a slot is restarted by software.
vendor_recommended_action: If the message shows up rarely and coincides with external events such as input power supplies being changed, this message can be safely ignored. If the message shows up continuously, contact your Cisco technical support representative.

vendor_message_text: Poe Health Check failed on slot [dec] (count = [dec])
vendor_explanation: The PoE health check has failed on a module. The PoE service provided by the module may be unavailable.
vendor_recommended_action: If the message shows up rarely and coincides with external events such as input power supplies being changed, this message can be safely ignored. If the message shows up continuously, contact your Cisco representative for a replacement of the PoE switching module.

vendor_message_text: Poe restarted on slot [dec] (count=[dec])
vendor_explanation: Software detected a glitch on the power input to the chassis power supplies and had to restart PoE on one or more slots.
vendor_recommended_action: Verify that the power provided to the switch conforms to Cisco's recommendations. If the power input to the chassis is good and the message is showing up continuously, contact your Cisco technical support representative.

vendor_message_text: Poe restarted for interfaces on slot [dec] (count=[dec])
vendor_explanation: Software detected a glitch on the power input to the chassis power supplies and had to restart PoE on the specified slot.
vendor_recommended_action: Verify that the power provided to the switch conforms to Cisco's recommendations. If the power input to the chassis is good and the message is showing up continuously, contact your Cisco technical support representative.

vendor_message_text: EvcSwitch: Service Instance cannot be created as  maximum limit  has already been reached.
vendor_explanation: The system limit on the maximum number of service instances has been reached. This includes all the user configured service instances and internal service instances.
vendor_recommended_action: If possible, delete other Service Instances or VLANs that are no longer in use.

vendor_message_text: EvcSwitch: There is not sufficient memory to allocate a new  Service Instance.
vendor_explanation: The software failed to allocate memory for a Service Instance. The specified service instance will not function but will appear in the configuration file. Other features and service instances are unaffected.
vendor_recommended_action: If possible, free up the available memory by removing features that are no longer in use.

vendor_message_text: All configured ACLs now fully loaded in hardware TCAM - hardware switching / QoS restored
vendor_explanation: All ACL-based features are now successfully loaded. Packets that were previously processed in software due to the prior loading failure will now be processed in hardware.Note If the features were policy maps, then QoS will be reenabled on all applicable interfaces.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: [char] [char] - now fully loaded in hardware
vendor_explanation: An ACL-based feature has now been successfully loaded after earlier failing to be fully programmed into hardware. Packets using this feature that were being processed in software due to the prior loading failure will now be processed in hardware. If the feature is a policy map, then QoS will be reenabled on the specific interface.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required. This log messages indicates a resumption of normal hardware-based ACL and QoS processing for the specified ACL-based feature

vendor_message_text: Failed to create CFM PortMac AclFeature for address   [mac-addr]  on port  [char]
vendor_explanation: The platform driver code failed to create a necessary data structure for enabling the CFM feature in the hardware. CFM will not operate correctly on the specified interface.
vendor_recommended_action: Remove other ACL or QoS-related configuration to free up resources, then disable and reenable CFM on the interface.

vendor_message_text: No more free labels available for path ([object-info])
vendor_explanation: A new label could not be assigned for an ACL that the user is trying to program. There are too many labels being used. As a result, software will apply security ACLs, and will not apply QoS features. It's possible too many distinct features using ACLs have been configured, or too many per-port per-VLAN features using ACLs have been configured. The hardware will forward the packets to the CPU for ACL processing.
vendor_recommended_action: Detaching and reattaching ACLs or policies may help in some cases.

vendor_message_text: Could not allocate path for ( [object-info])
vendor_explanation: There are too many ports or VLANs using ACLs. The ACLs might not work correctly.
vendor_recommended_action: Remove unnecessary ACLs from some interfaces.

vendor_message_text: Out of resources for Qos, permit all for [object-info]
vendor_explanation: The switch is running out of hardware CAM resources. All packets are permitted, and QoS is applied.
vendor_recommended_action: Remove unnecessary ACLs from some interfaces.

vendor_message_text: Output Port Acl  [char]100  has been disabled on port  [char]
vendor_explanation: The output port ACL is disabled on the interface because there are not enough hardware resources or there are ACEs that require CPU processing of packets.The port ACL is disabled and displays a warning message because the software cannot handle the output port ACLs.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Out of resources, punt packets to sw for [object-info]
vendor_explanation: The hardware content-addressable memory (CAM) resources have been depleted. The hardware forwards the packets to the software for ACL processing.
vendor_recommended_action: Remove unnecessary ACLs from some interfaces.

vendor_message_text: [char] failed diagnostics
vendor_explanation: An ASIC in slot [char] failed diagnostics.
vendor_recommended_action: Contact your technical support representative.

vendor_message_text: [char] port [dec] failed to send packet in [dec] tries
vendor_explanation: An ASIC in slot [char] was unable to send a loopback packet on port [dec] and this is the [dec]th time it tried to send and failed. This suggests that the switch is out of memory. The software will attempt to send a loopback packet only three times.
vendor_recommended_action: Contact your technical support representative.

vendor_message_text: [char] sent out a loopback packet on port [dec], but it came back on port [dec]
vendor_explanation: The ASIC diagnostics for slot [char] sent a loopback packet out port [dec] and it came back on another port [dec]. This is unexpected because the loopback is done within the hardware.
vendor_recommended_action: Contact your technical support representative.

vendor_message_text: [char] port [dec] lost a packet
vendor_explanation: A loopback packet was lost during online diagnostics of an ASIC in slot [char].
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: DHCP Snooping internal error [char]
vendor_explanation: A software sanity check failed in the DHCP snooping process. This message may also show up if the system is running out of memory or resources.
vendor_recommended_action: Reduce resource consumption by disabling features, ports, or packets destined to software. If the condition persists, call Cisco technical support.

vendor_message_text: DHCP snooping binding transfer failed. Unable to access URL.
vendor_explanation: The DHCP snooping binding transfer failed. The reason for failure can include any of the following:?he URL is not available to use.?ot enough memory is available for creating an agent.?he number of agents reached the maximum supported limit.?he switch is unable to create an agent.?he switch is unable to access the URL.?he switch is unable to start the agent.?he Abort timer expired.?he number of entries exceeded the maximum supported limit.?n error occurred when reading the remote database.?n error occurred while writing to the remote database.?HCP snooping expected more data during the read.?he string type is invalid.?he version string type is invalid.?HCP snooping is expecting a new line in the database.?TYPE' was not found in the remote database.?VERSION' was not found in the remote database.?BEGIN' was not found in the remote database.?END' was not found in the remote database.?he type string was not found in the remote database.?he version string was not found in the remote database.?he checksum failed upon entry into the remote database.
vendor_recommended_action: Based on the reason for the error (listed above), take the appropriate action.

vendor_message_text: DHCP snooping binding transfer failed ([dec]). [chars]
vendor_explanation: This message is logged once every 30 minutes and displays the [dec] number of failures that occurred for a given reason [chars] during the past 30 minutes.This message is a rate-limited version of the DHCP_SNOOPING-4-AGENT_OPERATION_FAILED message.
vendor_recommended_action: Based on the reason for the error [chars], look at the explanation for the DHCP_SNOOPING-4-AGENT_OPERATION_FAILED message, and take the appropriate action.

vendor_message_text: Saving DHCP snooping bindings to [char] can fill up your device causing the writes of bindings to device
vendor_explanation: Saving DHCP snooping bindings to a flash file system such as bootflash or slot0 could cause the flash to fill up. Possible consequences include a long delay to regain a console connection, write failures for database configurations, regular squeeze requirements, and reduced life of flash due to regular squeeze operations.
vendor_recommended_action: Save the DHCP snooping bindings to an alternate destination. Possible locations for the database agent include a TFTP or FTP server. See the command line help for a complete list of options.

vendor_message_text: DHCP Snooping received [dec] DHCP packets on interface [char]
vendor_explanation: DHCP snooping detected a DHCP packet rate-limit violation on the specified interface. The interface will be placed in the errdisable state.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: DHCP Snooping configuration may not take effect on secondary vlan [dec]. [char]
vendor_explanation: DHCP snooping configuration on the primary VLAN automatically propagates to all secondary VLANs if private VLANs are enabled.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: The interface [char] is receiving more than the threshold set
vendor_explanation: This message indicates that DHCP packets are coming into the CPU at a much higher rate than the specified threshold.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: The interface [char] has received a DHCP Release/Decline packet with no existing binding entry for it
vendor_explanation: This message indicates that a DHCP Release/Decline packet was received with no corresponding binding entry.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: IP source binding is configured on non existing vlan [dec].
vendor_explanation: IP source binding was configured on a VLAN that has not yet been configured.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required. It may persist unless you define the VLAN in question and then reapply the IP source binding. If you see this message regarding a VLAN that is correctly configured, contact your technical support representative.

vendor_message_text: IP source filter may not take effect on secondary vlan [dec] where IP source binding is configured. [char]
vendor_explanation: The IP source filter on the primary VLAN automatically propagates to all secondary VLANs if private VLANs are enabled.
vendor_recommended_action: Reconfigure the IP source binding to a known functioning VLAN.

vendor_message_text: NTP is not running; reloaded binding lease expiration times are incorrect.
vendor_explanation: If the DHCP snooping bindings are loaded by the DHCP snooping database agent and NTP is not running, then the calculated lease duration for the bindings will be incorrect.
vendor_recommended_action: Configure NTP on the switch to provide an accurate time and date for the system clock. Then disable and re-enable DHCP snooping to clear the bindings database.

vendor_message_text: The interface [char] is not able to insert opt82 into the packet because of insufficient space in the packet
vendor_explanation: This message indicates that certain data was not inserted into a DHCP packet due t o insufficient space in the packet.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Fail to enqueue DHCP packet into processing queue: [char]
vendor_explanation: DHCP packets are coming into the CPU at a much higher rate than the DHCP snooping process can handle them. These unhandled DHCP packets will be dropped to prevent a denial of service attack.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Error is encountered in processing acknowledgement for DHCP snooping binding sync [char]. ack message txn id:[hex]
vendor_explanation: There was an error in handling the DHCP synchronization acknowledgement. In most of these cases, the ACK message is ignored.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: DHCP snooping binding transfer failed on the Standby Supervisor. [char]
vendor_explanation: If the DHCP snooping database supporting SSO is configured as a local device, both supervisor engines will update their database whenever there is an update regarding bindings. This error message is an indication that a snooping database update on the standby supervisor engine failed in the manner mentioned. The most likely cause for these problems is if the snooping database is configured as a slot0 device, but functioning compact flash memory is only present on the active supervisor engine's slot0 while the standby supervisor engine's slot0 is empty or faulty. Possible variations in output include:"URL not available for use.""Not enough memory available for creating agent.""Number of agents reached maximum supported limit.""Unable to create agent.""Unable to access URL.""Unable to start agent.""Abort timer expiry.""Number of entries exceeded max supported limit.""Unable to transfer bindings. Memory allocation failure.""Error reading the remote database.""Error writing to remote database.""Expected more data on read.""Type string invalid.""Version string invalid.""New line expected in database.""\'TYPE\' not found in remote database.""\'VERSION\' not found in remote database.""\'BEGIN \' not found in remote database.""\'END\' not found in remote database.""Type string not found in remote database.""Version string not found in remote database.""Checksum failed on an entry in remote database.""No failure recorded."
vendor_recommended_action: The switch will continue to function if no action is taken, but the redundancy features will be compromised until both active and standby supervisor engines have working flash memory available. Replace or insert flash memory into the supervisor engine that lacks it if needed.

vendor_message_text: [char] drop message with mismatched source interface the binding is not updated message type: [char] MAC sa: [mac-addr]
vendor_explanation: The DHCP snooping feature has detected a host trying to carry out a denial of service attack on another host in the network. The packet will be dropped.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: [char] drop message because the chaddr doesn't match source mac message type: [char] chaddr: [mac-addr] MAC sa: [mac-addr]
vendor_explanation: The DHCP snooping feature attempted MAC address validation and the check failed. There may be a malicious host trying to carry out a denial of service attack on the DHCP server. The packet will be dropped.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: [char] drop message with non-zero giaddr or option82 value on untrusted port message type: [char] MAC sa: [mac-addr]
vendor_explanation: The DHCP snooping feature discovered a DHCP packet with option values not allowed on the untrusted port, indicating some host may be trying to act as a DHCP relay or server. The packet will be dropped.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: [char] drop message on untrusted port message type: [char] MAC sa: [mac-addr]
vendor_explanation: The DHCP snooping feature discovered certain types of DHCP messages not allowed on the untrusted interface, indicating some host may be trying to act as a DHCP server. The packet will be dropped.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: DHCP snooping database [char] succeeded.
vendor_explanation: DHCP snooping has successfully read or written to the database.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Binding collision. [dec] bindings ignored
vendor_explanation: One or more bindings from the database file has a MAC address and VLAN combination for which the switch already holds DHCP snooping bindings.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Interface not valid. [dec] bindings ignored.
vendor_explanation: The interface that is listed in the database file's binding is not available, that the interface is a router port, or that the interface is a DHCP snooping-trusted Layer 2 interface.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Lease Expired. [dec] bindings ignored.
vendor_explanation: The DHCP lease expired for the given number of bindings from the database file.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Parsing failed for [dec] bindings.
vendor_explanation: The database read operation failed for the stated number of bindings.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Vlan not supported. [dec] bindings ignored.
vendor_explanation: The VLAN is not supported by DHCP snooping.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Memory was not available to perform the 802.1X action
vendor_explanation: Due to a lack of memory 802.1X cannot perform authentication, so it will not be enabled.
vendor_recommended_action: Reduce other system activity to ease memory demands. Install more memory, if necessary.

vendor_message_text: DOT1X unable to start
vendor_explanation: For unknown reasons 802.1X cannot start.
vendor_recommended_action: Restart 802.1X by entering the dot1x system-auth-control command in case the condition is transient. If the restart fails, reload the device.

vendor_message_text: An unknown operational error occurred
vendor_explanation: Due to an unexpected internal error 802.1X cannot operate.
vendor_recommended_action: Reload the device.

vendor_message_text: Authentication failed for client ([char]) on Interface [char]
vendor_explanation: Authentication was unsuccessful.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Authentication successful for client ([char]) on Interface [char]
vendor_explanation: Authentication was successful.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Memory not available to perform the trunk negotiation action
vendor_explanation: The system is unable to negotiate trunks because of a lack of memory.
vendor_recommended_action: Reduce other system activity to ease memory demands. If necessary, upgrade to a larger memory configuration.

vendor_message_text: An internal timer error occurred when trunking on interface [char]
vendor_explanation: Occasionally a timer used by the trunking protocol expires unexpectedly. This problem is corrected internally.
vendor_recommended_action: This problem has no long-term ramifications. However, if further trunking problems persist, you should reload the device.

vendor_message_text: An unknown operational error occurred
vendor_explanation: The system is unable to negotiate trunks because an internal operation generated an error that the protocol (DTP, in this case) did not expect to handle.
vendor_recommended_action: Reload the device.

vendor_message_text: Unable to perform trunk negotiation on port [char] because of VTP domain mismatch.
vendor_explanation: The two ports involved in trunk negotiation belong to different VTP domains. Trunking is possible only when the ports involved belong to the same VTP domain.
vendor_recommended_action: Reconfigure the switch to ensure that the two ports that are involved in trunk negotiation belong to the same VTP domain.

vendor_message_text: Illegal config (on, isl--on,dot1q) on <mod/port>
vendor_explanation: The two ports on the link are set to the ON mode, but one is set to 802.1Q encapsulation, while the other is set to ISL encapsulation. When both ports on a link are set to the ON mode, their encapsulation types must match.
vendor_recommended_action: Configure both ports on the link to have the same encapsulation type.

vendor_message_text: Port [dec]/[chars] has become non-trunk
vendor_explanation: The interface [dec] / [chars] is nontrunked. [dec] / [chars] is the module number/interface range.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Port [dec]/[chars] has changed from [chars] trunk to [chars] trunk
vendor_explanation: The encapsulation type of the trunk changed. [dec] is the module number, the first [chars] is the interface number, the second [chars] is the original encapsulation type, and the third [chars] is the new encapsulation type.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Port [dec]/[chars] has become trunk
vendor_explanation: Interface [dec] / [chars] is trunked. [dec] / [chars] is the module number/interface range.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: No EbmPort memory to allocate EbmPort for PimPort [char]
vendor_explanation: There is insufficient memory for information that is associated with the specified port.
vendor_recommended_action: Install additional memory.

vendor_message_text: Cannot allocate memory for host checkpoint message. Layer2 host redundancy on standby will be out-of-sync with active.
vendor_explanation: There is insufficient memory to allocate space for this internal data structure.
vendor_recommended_action: You may need to install additional memory in both supervisor engines.

vendor_message_text: No interposition table memory to add entry for addr %ea
vendor_explanation: There is insufficient memory for this internal data structure.
vendor_recommended_action: Install additional memory.

vendor_message_text: No igmp group memory to add new group entry for addr [mac-addr]
vendor_explanation: This error occurs if you have created a large number of IGMP groups and there is insufficient memory to support additional Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP) group entries.
vendor_recommended_action: Either install additional memory, or reduce the number of IGMP groups.

vendor_message_text: No port host table memory to add entry for addr [mac-addr] / [mac-addr]
vendor_explanation: There is insufficient memory for this internal data structure.
vendor_recommended_action: Install additional memory.

vendor_message_text: No vlan group table memory to add entry for addr %ea
vendor_explanation: There is insufficient memory to support additional Layer 2 group entries corresponding to IP multicast groups.
vendor_recommended_action: Install additional memory. If memory is unavailable, turn off Cisco Group Management Protocol (CGMP)/Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP).

vendor_message_text: No vlan host table memory to add entry for addr %ea
vendor_explanation: There is insufficient memory to support additional host addresses.
vendor_recommended_action: Install additional memory.

vendor_message_text: Host [mac-addr] in vlan [dec] is flapping between port [char] and port [char]
vendor_explanation: The specified host is detected as a source address on multiple ports. Typically, a host is supposed to be learned on only one port. A spanning tree loop is the most common cause of this condition. All traffic from the specified host is temporarily dropped. After 15 seconds, forwarding is reenabled. If the problem persists, the traffic from the problem host continues to be dropped indefinitely. As of Cisco IOS release 12.2(52)SG, this message is enabled by the mac address-table notification mac-move comand. By default, the message is disabled. If enabled, this message will be displayed whenever a host moves. To reflect the change, the text of this syslog message changes to C4K_EBM-4-HOSTFLAPPING:Host %ea in vlan %d is moving from port %s to port %s.
vendor_recommended_action: Make sure that spanning tree is enabled to prevent spanning tree loops. If you have spanning tree disabled, make sure that you have no spanning tree loops in your network.

vendor_message_text: Backlog of checkpoint message waiting to be synced to standby has exceeded pre-defined limits. The host table may become out-of-sync with active.
vendor_explanation: The active supervisor engine is overloaded and unable to synchronize host messages to the standby supervisor engine or the standby supervisor engine is not in the proper state.
vendor_recommended_action: Examine syslog messages from the active supervisor engine and standby supervisor engine to determine if any errors have been reported.

vendor_message_text: Backlog of host age checkpoint message waiting to be sent to active has exceeded pre-defined limits.  The host table may become out-of-sync with active.
vendor_explanation: The active is overloaded and unable to delete age host messages it received from standby or the standby is not in the proper state.
vendor_recommended_action: Examine syslog messages from active and standby to determine if any errors have been reported. Copy the error message exactly as it appears on the console or in the system log. Research and attempt to resolve the error using the Output Interpreter https://www.cisco.com/cgi-bin/Support/OutputInterpreter/home.pl. Issue the show tech-support command to gather data that may help identify the nature of the error. Also perform a search of the Bug Toolkit http://www.cisco.com/cgi-bin/Support/Bugtool/home.pl. If you still require assistance, open a case with the Technical Assistance Center via the Internet http://tools.cisco.com/ServiceRequestTool/create/launch.do, or contact your Cisco technical support.

vendor_message_text: Filtering Ethernet MAC address of value zero from agent host table interface (port: [char])
vendor_explanation: The switch received a packet with the MAC address 00:00:00:00:00:00. This MAC address is not valid and was probably generated by some non-IEEE 802.1D-compliant hardware or software in the network.The host sort algorithm does not sort hosts with MAC addresses that have all zeros (00:00:00:00:00:00), because a MAC address that has all zeros can not be listed in the learned host table. A request to show learned hosts, either by the show cam dynamic command or by an SNMP request, does not list a MAC address that has all zeros.
vendor_recommended_action: Track the source of the invalid MAC address because it might cause other problems.

vendor_message_text: Routed port channels cannot be  created while the switch is configured in the SSO redundancy mode
vendor_explanation: Routed port channels are not supported while the switch is configured in the SSO redundancy mode.
vendor_recommended_action: Switch to RPR mode or use an SVI in a VLAN where a layer 2 port channel is the only member.

vendor_message_text: Not enough memory available for [char]
vendor_explanation: The Port Aggregation Protocol or EtherChannel cannot obtain the memory it needs.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Interface [char] joined port-channel [char]
vendor_explanation: The interface has joined the bundle.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Aggregator limit reached
vendor_explanation: A new aggregator cannot be allocated in the group.
vendor_recommended_action: Change the port attributes of the ports in the group so that they match and join the same aggregator.

vendor_message_text: Port-channel [char] is down
vendor_explanation: The administrative state of the aggregation port channel is down. The port remains in a standalone state until the state of the aggregation port is up.
vendor_recommended_action: Ensure that all of the ports in the bundle have the same configuration.

vendor_message_text: [char] is not compatible with [char] and will be suspended ([char])
vendor_explanation: The port has different port attributes from those of the port channel (or the ports within the port channel).
vendor_recommended_action: Adjust the port attributes to match those of the port channel.

vendor_message_text: [char] is not compatible with aggregators in channel [dec] and cannot attach to them ([char])
vendor_explanation: This port has different port attributes than other ports within the port channel.
vendor_recommended_action: Match the port attributes to that of the port channel.

vendor_message_text: Removed [char] from port channel because a QoS policy cannot be supported across multiple DFC cards.
vendor_explanation: The port that is specified in the error message cannot join a port channel because the QoS policy that is attached to the port channel cannot support multiple DFC cards.
vendor_recommended_action: Place the port in another port channel, or remove the QoS policy from the port channel.

vendor_message_text: Removed [char] from port channel  as QoS attributes of port and port-channel are different.
vendor_explanation: The Port specified in the error message cannot join port channel, because the QoS attributes of this port are not consistent with the QoS attributes of the port-channel.
vendor_recommended_action: Match the QoS attributes of the specified port to the QoS attributes of other member ports in the port channel. Use the show queueing interface command to display the QoS attributes of a port.

vendor_message_text: [char] is compatible with port-channel members
vendor_explanation: The specified interface is not operational because its attributes are different from the attributes of the port channel or the attributes of the interfaces within the port channel. The switch detects that the attributes of the specified port now match the port-channel attributes.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: [char] suspended: incompatible remote port  with [char]
vendor_explanation: The configuration of the remote port is different from the configuration of the other ports in the bundle. A port can join the bundle only when the global configuration of the port and the configuration of the remote port are the same as the other ports in the bundle.
vendor_recommended_action: Ensure that the configuration of the remote ports is the same for all ports in the bundle.

vendor_message_text: Channel protocol mismatch for interface [char] in group [dec]: the interface can not be added to the channel group
vendor_explanation: The interface cannot be added to the channel group with the specified mode.
vendor_recommended_action: Change the channel group or the mode for the interface.

vendor_message_text: Command rejected: the interface [char] is already part of a channel with a different type of protocol enabled
vendor_explanation: The interface cannot be selected for the specified protocol because it is already part of a channel with a different type of protocol enabled.
vendor_recommended_action: Remove the interface from the channel group.

vendor_message_text: Command rejected: the interface [char] is already part of a channel
vendor_explanation: The interface cannot be unselected for the specified protocol because it is already part of a channel.
vendor_recommended_action: Remove the interface from the channel group.

vendor_message_text: [char] suspended: PAgP not enabled on the remote port.
vendor_explanation: PAgP is enabled on the Layer 3 interface, but the remote port does not have PAgP enabled. In this mode, the port is put in a suspended state.
vendor_recommended_action: Enable PAgP on the remote side.

vendor_message_text: [char] suspended: LACP currently not enabled on the remote port.
vendor_explanation: LACP is enabled on a Layer 3 interface, but the remote port does not have LACP enabled. In this mode, the port is put in a suspended state.
vendor_recommended_action: Enable LACP on the remote side.

vendor_message_text: Port-channel [char] is up as its  bundled ports ([dec]) meets min-links
vendor_explanation: The administrative configuration of minimum links is equal or less than the number of bundled ports. Therefore this port channel has been brought up.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Port-channel [char] is down  bundled ports ([dec]) doesn't meet min-links
vendor_explanation: The administrative configuration of minimum links is greater than the number of bundled ports. Therefore this port channel has been brought down.
vendor_recommended_action: Reduce the min-links configuration for this group or add more ports to this port-channel to create a bundle.

vendor_message_text: Invalid EC mode
vendor_explanation: LACP is not included in the image. You cannot set EC mode to active or passive.
vendor_recommended_action: Upgrade to an image with LACP, or set the mode to On.

vendor_message_text: Invalid EC mode
vendor_explanation: PAgP is not included in the image, so the EtherChannel mode cannot be set to desirable/auto.
vendor_recommended_action: Obtain an image that includes PAgP, or set the mode to ON.

vendor_message_text: Shutting down [char] as its port-channel is admin-down
vendor_explanation: The administrative state of the aggregate port is down, which forces the administrative state of the port to also be down. The administrative state of the port is controlled by the administrative state of its aggregate port.
vendor_recommended_action: Enter the no shutdown command on the aggregate port to activate the aggregation port.

vendor_message_text: [char] will remain down as its port-channel [char] is admin-down
vendor_explanation: An interface with EtherChannel configuration cannot be administratively up if its port channel is administratively down. Although this interface has an EtherChannel configuration, it has no information about the port channel. The no shutdown command is not supported.
vendor_recommended_action: Wait for the module to come online.

vendor_message_text: Interface [char] left the port-channel [char]
vendor_explanation: The interface fell off the bundle.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: [char] will not join any port-channel
vendor_explanation: The configurations for PortFast, VMPS, and Dest-SPAN are incompatible with EtherChannel.
vendor_recommended_action: Unconfigure the three features so that the port can form a bundle.

vendor_message_text: [char] MAC was reset due to a fatal Rx error
vendor_explanation: There was an Rx error with the specified port, and the port's MAC was reset.
vendor_recommended_action: If this continues to happen, please contact Cisco Technical Support representative to possibly replace the supervisor.

vendor_message_text: [char]: Invalid Edc Vendor Type: [dec]
vendor_explanation: An invalid EDC has been detected in the module.
vendor_recommended_action: Try resetting the module. If the message recurs, return the module for repair.

vendor_message_text: Non-SFP+ inserted in port [char], which is for 10G SFP+ OneX Converter
vendor_explanation: A non-SFP+ transceiver was inserted into a OneX X2-SFP+ converter. Currently, the OneX converter can only support the SFP+ 10G transceiver, not a traditional 1G SFP transceiver.
vendor_recommended_action: Remove the faulty SFP-form transceiver immediately and insert a valid Cisco SFP+ 10G transceiver instead; if an SFP transceiver must be used, please use the: "hw-module module <n> port-group <m> select gigabitethernet" command to convert the X2 port into a TwinGig port, then remove the OneX converter and insert a TwinGig Module converter instead.

vendor_message_text: Port [char]: SFP+ on OneX Converter's seeprom is bad, try reinserting: vendor: [char], p/n: [char], s/n: [char]
vendor_explanation: An SFP Converter was detected, and the read of its serial EEPROM succeeded, but the SFP module appears invalid (perhaps due to a bad checksum). This could happen because an SFP is inserted where an SFP+ is expected. The message tells the vendor, part number and serial number read from the Converter's serial EEPROM.
vendor_recommended_action: Remove SFP and insert a supported 10G SFP+ module.

vendor_message_text: Port([char]) detected something unsupported inserted in X2 hole The OneX Converter on port [char] detected an unsupported EDC type
vendor_explanation: Informational message only. An unsupported pluggable has been detected in OneX converter
vendor_recommended_action: No action is required.

vendor_message_text: Port([char]) detected something unsupported inserted in X2 hole
vendor_explanation: Informational message only. An unsupported pluggable has been detected in X2 hole.
vendor_recommended_action: No action is required.

vendor_message_text: Port [char]: OneX converter inserted: vendor: [char], p/n: [char], s/n: [char] [char]
vendor_explanation: A OneX Converter was detected and its serial EEPROM read. The message shows the vendor, part number, and serial number from the OneX Converter's serial EEPROM.
vendor_recommended_action: No action is required.

vendor_message_text: Port [char] OneX converter removed
vendor_explanation: A OneX Converter was removed from the specified X2 port.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only. No action is required.

vendor_message_text: Port [char]: SFP+ on OneX Converter inserted: vendor: [char], p/n: [char], s/n: [char]
vendor_explanation: An SFP+ was detected in a OneX Converter and the SFP+ serial EEPROM read. The message shows the vendor, part number, and serial number from SFP+ EEPROM.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an information message only. No action is required.

vendor_message_text: Port [char]: SFP+ on OneX Converter removed
vendor_explanation: An SFP+ was removed from a OneX Converter on the specified X2 port.

vendor_message_text: Port [char] X2 pluggable removed

vendor_recommended_action: No action is required.

vendor_message_text: [char]: Link Monitor detects Link state marginal, but go ahead to link up

vendor_recommended_action: If this problem is seen repeatedly, please double check the cable and its length to meet those cabling requirements. Also, please consider cable mitigation technique to improve the quality of the link. If port is in this state, you might see possible packet loss.

vendor_message_text: PoE did not properly initialize for module [dec].
vendor_explanation: Power over Ethernet did not initialize properly.
vendor_recommended_action: Reset the module. If the problem persists, contact Cisco TAC.

vendor_message_text: Module %u POE controller has detected a stall
vendor_explanation: A problem has been detected with one or more Power Over Ethernet controllers on the module.
vendor_recommended_action: Current POE settings should remain stable but no changes to POE can be made. The module should be reset at the next maintenance window to restore full POE functionality.

vendor_message_text: Module %u POE controller has been shutdown because of excessive power usage.
vendor_explanation: Power over Ethernet to the module has shut down because it drew too much power.
vendor_recommended_action: Remove some devices. Verify that the power consumption is not over limit. Reset the module.

vendor_message_text: Inline powered device connected on port [char] exceeded its [char] threshold.
vendor_explanation: This message might be caused by a faulty powered device drawing more power than is allocated.
vendor_recommended_action: Verify that the powered device on the port is functioning properly and only drawing the configured power using the show power module command.

vendor_message_text: Failed to read seeprom on port [char]. Reinsert X2 module or configure GigabitEthernet port group if TwinGigConverter is installed.
vendor_explanation: A pluggable has been detected in the TenGig port referred to in the message, but the read of its serial eeprom failed. Sometimes, the read fails because the X2 is not seated correctly. Seeprom read can also fail if the interface is in 10G mode and TwinGigConverter is inserted in the hole.
vendor_recommended_action:
If TwinGigConverter is inserted, remove the TwinGigConverter or reconfigure the port using the command hw-module module port-group

select gigabitethernet. If an X2 is inserted, try removing and re-inserting. If this message still appears, try the X2 in another port. If the X2 fails in another port, call TAC for further troubleshooting. If the X2 succeeds in other ports, the original port may be bad. Call TAC for further troubleshooting.

vendor_message_text: Cannot find compact flash
vendor_explanation: You may see this message if the compact flash is not inserted properly or if it is removed while the switch is trying to access the flash.
vendor_recommended_action: Reinsert the compact flash and retry the operation.

vendor_message_text: Compact flash is not ready
vendor_explanation: You may see this message if the compact flash is not inserted properly or if it is removed while the switch is trying to access the flash.
vendor_recommended_action: Reinsert the compact flash and retry the operation.

vendor_message_text: No bridge-domain host table memory to add entry for addr [mac-addr]
vendor_explanation: There is insufficient memory left to support additional host addresses. Previously learnt host addresses are unaffected.

vendor_message_text: Host [mac-addr] in bridge-domain [dec] is flapping between port [char] and port [char]
vendor_explanation: The specified host is being seen as a source address on multiple ports. Normally, a host is only supposed to be learned on one port. The most common cause of this condition is spanning tree loops.
vendor_recommended_action: Please make arrangements such that the same MAC address does not appear in multiple service instances in a short time interval.

vendor_message_text: GbmSwitch: There is not sufficient memory to create the  required BridgeDomain.
vendor_explanation: The software failed to allocate memory for the required Bridge Domain. The specified bridge domain will not fuction but will appear in the configuration file. Other features and bridge domains are unaffected.

vendor_message_text: GbmSwitch: There is not sufficient memory to allocate
vendor_explanation: The software failed to allocate memory for a Service Instance (PseudoPort). The specified service instance will not function but will appear in the configuration file. Other features and service instances are unaffected.
vendor_recommended_action: If possible, free up available memory by unconfiguring features that are no longer in use.

vendor_message_text: With the addition of  [mac-addr]  on  [char]   the MAC Table has been exhausted.

vendor_message_text: Memory for constructing ACLs is not available.

vendor_message_text: Non-SFP+ inserted in port [char], which is for 10G SFP+ OneX Converter
vendor_explanation: A non-SFP+ transceiver is inserted into a OneX X2-SFP+ converter. Currently, a OneX converter can only support an SFP+ 10G transceiver, not a traditional 1G SFP transceiver.
vendor_recommended_action: Remove the faulty SFP-form transceiver immediately and insert a valid Cisco SFP+ 10G transceiver instead.

vendor_message_text: Port [char]: OneX Converter's seeprom is bad, try reinserting: vendor: [char], p/n: [char], s/n: [char]
vendor_explanation: A OneX converter was detected, and the read of its serial EEPROM succeeded, but the contents are invalid (perhaps due to a bad checksum). This event can occur because the OneX converter is not seated correctly. The message shows the vendor, part number, and serial number read from the converter's serial EEPROM.
vendor_recommended_action: Try removing and reinserting the OneX converter. If this message still appears after that action, try inserting the converter in another port to verify that the converter is bad, not the port. If the converter fails in another port, return the converter. If the converter succeeds in other ports, it implies that the original port is bad, not the converter, and that the module needs to be returned. As a further test of the original port, try other OneX converters. If these other OneX converters also fail in that port, it is very likely that the port is bad.

vendor_message_text: Port [char]: Sfp on OneX Converter's seeprom is bad, try reinserting: vendor: [char], p/n: [char], s/n: [char]
vendor_explanation: An SFP converter was detected, and the read of its serial EEPROM succeeded, but the SFP module used was invalid for the application. This event can occur because an SFP was used where an SFP+ was expected. The message shows the vendor, part number, and serial number read from the converter's serial EEPROM.
vendor_recommended_action: Try removing the 1-G SFP and inserting a valid 10-G SFP+ module.

vendor_message_text: Port [char]: TwinGig Converter's seeprom is bad, try reinserting: vendor: [char], p/n: [char], s/n: [char]
vendor_explanation: A TwinGig Converter has been detected, and the read of its serial EEPROM succeeded, but the contents are invalid (possibly a bad checksum). This could happen because the TwinGig Converter is not seated correctly. The message tells the vendor, part number and serial number read from the Converter's serial EEPROM.
vendor_recommended_action: Try removing and reinserting the TwinGig Converter. If this message still appears after that, try the Converter in another port, to verify that the Converter is bad, and not the port. If the Converter fails in another port, return the Converter. If the Converter succeeds in other ports, it implies that the original port is bad, not the Converter, and the module needs to be returned. As a further test of the original port, other TwinGig Converters could be tried. If these other TwinGig Converters also fail in that port, it is very likely that the port is bad.

vendor_message_text: Port [char]: TwinGig Converter integrity check failed: bad crc
vendor_explanation: Only Cisco-qualified TwinGig Converters are supported. Others show as unsupported and cause the associated port to placed in faulty status. The CRC of the TwinGig Converter's SEEPROM is invalid.
vendor_recommended_action: Verify that the TwinGig Converter is from a Cisco-qualified source. If it is, try reinserting it. If the message still appears after that, try it in another port, to verify the Converter is bad, and not the port. If it still produces error messages, replace the TwinGig Converter.

vendor_message_text: Port [char]: Failed to identify TwinGig Converter
vendor_explanation: Something is inserted in the specified port, which has been configured to accept a TwinGig Converter, an adaptor which converts an X2 port into 2 SFP ports, but it has failed the identification process.
vendor_recommended_action: If the object inserted in the port isn't a TwinGig Converter, remove it. If it is a TwinGig Converter, try removing and reinserting it. If the message still appears after that, try it in another port, to verify the Converter is bad, and not the port. If the Converter fails in another port, return it.

vendor_message_text: Port [char]: TwinGig Converter integrity check failed: bad key
vendor_explanation: Only Cisco-qualified TwinGig Converters are supported. Others show as unsupported and cause the associated ports to be placed in faulty status.
vendor_recommended_action: Replace the TwinGig Converter with a Cisco-qualified one.

vendor_message_text: Port [char]: S2w error while reading status of TwinGig Converter
vendor_explanation: Internal communication error when reading TwinGig Converter status data.
vendor_recommended_action: Remove and reinsert the TwinGig Converter. If that doesn't solve the problem, try using the hw-module module port-group command to change to ten gigabit mode and back to gigabit mode, to reset things.

vendor_message_text: Port [char]: Failed to read serial eeprom of TwinGig Converter, try reinserting
vendor_explanation: A TwinGig Converter has been detected in the X2 port referred to in the message, but the read of its serial eeprom failed. Sometimes the read fails because the TwinGig Converter is not seated correctly.
vendor_recommended_action: Try removing and reinserting the TwinGig Converter. If this message still appears after that, try the Converter in another port, to verify that the Converter is bad, and not the port. If the Converter fails in another port, return the Converter. If the Converter succeeds in other ports, it implies that the original port is bad, not the Converter, and the module needs to be returned. As a further test of the original port, other TwinGig Converters could be tried. If these other TwinGig Converters also fail in that port, it is very likely that the port is bad.

vendor_message_text: TwinGigConverter inserted in port [char], which is configured for X2
vendor_explanation: A TwinGig converter was inserted into an port which was configured for an X2 module.
vendor_recommended_action:
Remove the TwinGig module or reconfigure the port for gigabit Ethernet, using the hw-module module port-group

select gigabitethernet command.

vendor_message_text: X2 inserted in port [char], which is configured for a TwinGigConverter
vendor_explanation: An X2 transceiver has been inserted into an port which has been configured to accept a TwinGig Converter, an adaptor which converts an X2 port into 2 SFP ports. The X2 is a ten gigabit transceiver, and SFPs are gigabit transceivers.
vendor_recommended_action: Remove the X2, or reconfigure the port to ten gigabit, using the hw-module module <m> port-group select tengigabitethernet command.

vendor_message_text: Port [char]: X2Pluggable's seeprom is bad, try reinserting: vendor: [char], p/n: [char], s/n: [char]
vendor_explanation: An X2 pluggable has been detected, and the read of its serial EEPROM succeeded, but the contents are invalid (perhaps bad checksum). This event could possibly happen because the X2 module is not seated correctly. The message tells the vendor, part number and serial number read from the module's serial EEPROM.
vendor_recommended_action: Try removing and reinserting the X2 module. If this message still appears after that, try the module in another port, to verify that the module is bad, and not the port. If the module fails in another port, return the module. If the module succeeds in other ports, it implies that the original port is bad, not the converter, and the module needs to be returned. As a further test of the original port, other X2 modules could be tried. If these other X2 modules also fail in that port, it is very likely that the port is bad.

vendor_message_text: Failed to read seeprom on port [char]. Reinsert X2 module or configure GigabitEthernet port group if TwinGigConverter is installed.
vendor_explanation: A pluggable has been detected in the TenGig port referred to in the message, but the read of its serial eeprom failed. It could be that the X2 is not seated correctly. A SEEPROM read can also fail if the interface is in 10G mode and a TwinGig Converter is inserted.
vendor_recommended_action:
If a TwinGig Converter is inserted, remove the TwinGig Converter or reconfigure the port using the hw-module module port-group

select gigabitethernet command. If an X2 is inserted, try removing and re-inserting the X2. If this message still appears, try the X2 in another port. If the X2 fails in another port, call TAC for further troubleshooting. If the X2 succeeds in other ports, the original port may be bad.

vendor_message_text: Port [char]: TwinGig Converter is unsupported
vendor_explanation: The TwinGig Converter was identified as not a Cisco-qualified Converter.
vendor_recommended_action: If this TwinGig Converter was purchased from Cisco, contact Cisco TAC to get it replaced.

vendor_explanation: A label pair could not be allocated for the specified path. This can happen because the label supply is exhausted, or because the profile supply is exhausted, or because the path requires the application of mutually-incompatible features. Packets that traverse this path will be processed in software.Note If the path includes QoS, it will be disabled on the interface.
vendor_recommended_action: Simplify the configuration to reduce the number of labels and profiles required, or remove the conflicting features.

vendor_message_text: DFE timeout: [char]

vendor_explanation: Transmit queues of ports on a switching module pool did not drain and queue space was not released. The pool may not map exactly to a slot. If this happened in response to a policy configuration, the new policy does not take effect. If it happened with the insertion of a switching module, the module cannot be used to transmit traffic.

vendor_message_text: Blocked transmit queue HwTxQId[dec] on [char], count=[dec]
vendor_explanation: This rate-limited message indicates that a transmit queue and traffic on a port is blocked. You may see the blocked transmit queue message if the supervisor engine is not able to send packets to the switching module because it received a busy bit from the switching module. A hardware failure or a speed/duplex mismatch can cause this problem.
vendor_recommended_action: Configure both sides of the link to autonegotiate for speed and duplex. Check if pause is in effect, resulting in the queue being blocked, Issue the shut/no shut command to recover the port. If the problem persists, move the connected device to another port and see if the problem happens there. If neither of these solves the problem, issue the hw-module reset command in order to reboot the switch and reset the line card.

vendor_message_text: [char] Tx-Queue could be blocked due to duplex mismatch or receiving excessive pause frames
vendor_explanation: The TxQueue on this port could be blocked due to a duplex mismatch or from receiving too many pause frames.
vendor_recommended_action: Use the show interface <name> count all command to verify the excessive collisions and pause frame counters. Duplex mismatch problems can be fixed by configuring both ends of a link in auto-negotiate mode. It can also be fixed by turning off auto-negotiation on both ends of the link and ensuring that the duplex configuration on both ends is the same. Excessive pause frames are not expected under normal conditions. If they occur, investigate on the other end of the link to address the problem. After fixing the problem, the port's TxQueue status can be checked by using the show platform hardware interface <name> tx command. The results will indicate whether one or more TxQueue's on this port are still stuck or working properly. If this message is seen when the duplex settings are correct, contact your technical support representative.

vendor_message_text: Blocking [char] on [char]. Inconsistent peer vlan.
vendor_explanation: The spanning tree port (with spanning-tree port ID [char]) that is associated with the listed instance and interface is held in blocking state until the port VLAN ID (PVID) inconsistency is resolved. The listed spanning tree instance is that of the native VLAN ID of the interface on the peer switch to which the listed interface is connected.

vendor_recommended_action: Locate the misconfigured local ports by entering the show interfaces status err-disabled command. Check the EtherChannel configuration on the remote device by entering the show etherchannel summary command on the remote device. vendor_message_text: Loop guard blocking port [char] on [char].

vendor_recommended_action: Use the show spanning-tree inconsistentports command to review the list of interfaces with loop guard inconsistencies. Determine why devices that are connected to the listed ports are not sending BPDUs. One reason could be that they do not run the Spanning Tree Protocol; in this case, you should disable loop guard in the inconsistent interfaces or start the Spanning Tree Protocol on the other side of the links, depending on the context. Another reason could be a failure in the cable. If the link has a failure that makes it unidirectional (you can transmit, but you cannot receive), you should replace the old cable with a new cable.

vendor_message_text: Loop guard [char] on port [char].

When enabled, the interface will be put into blocking state and marked as loop guard inconsistent when the message age timer expires because no BPDUs were received from the designated bridge. This feature is used to detect unidirectional links.
vendor_recommended_action: Verify that this is the desired configuration for the listed interface. Correct it if this is not the desired configuration; otherwise, no further action is required.

vendor_message_text: Loop guard unblocking port [char] on [char].
vendor_explanation: The listed interface received a BPDU, and if the inconsistency was due to an unidirectional link failure, the problem does not exist anymore. The loop guard inconsistency is cleared for the interface, which is taken out of the blocking state.
vendor_recommended_action: This is an informational message only; no action is required.

vendor_message_text: Blocking [char] port [char]: Inconsitent [char] PVST BPDU received on VLAN [dec]
vendor_explanation: When a PVST+ switch is connected to an MST switch, the CIST (MSTOO) becomes the root for all PVST+ spanning trees. Looping occurs if any PVST+ spanning tree has a root with a better preference than IST. To prevent looping, the port, which is on the MST switch that receives the superior message from the PVST+ side, is blocked by root guard.When STP is converging after a new switch or a switch port is added to the topology, this condition occurs transiently. The port unblocks automatically in such cases.
vendor_recommended_action: If the port remains blocked, identify the root bridge as reported in the message, and configure a worse priority for the VLAN spanning tree. There could be better PVST roots than the message indicates, and the port will not recover until all such roots are cleared. If you are unsure whether the roots are cleared, disable and enable the port again.

vendor_message_text: Port [char]: Transceiver's seeprom is bad, try reinserting: vendor: [char], p/n: [char], s/n: [char]
vendor_explanation: A transceiver with a serial EEPROM has been detected in the port referred to in the message, and the read of the serial EEPROM's contents succeeded, but the contents are not valid (perhaps there was a bad checksum). The message tells the vendor, part number and serial number it read from the transceiver's serial EEPROM. This event could possibly happen because the transceiver is not seated correctly.
vendor_recommended_action: Try removing and reinserting the transceiver. If this message still appears after that, try the transceiver in another port, to verify that the transceiver is bad, and not the port. If the transceiver fails in another port, return the transceiver, as the transceiver must be reprogrammed for it to work. If the transceiver succeeds in other ports, but not the original port, that implies that the original port is bad, not the transceiver, and the module needs to be returned, to fix the port. As a further test of the port, other transceivers could be tried in the suspected bad port. If these other transceivers also fail in that port, it is very likely that the port is bad.

vendor_message_text: Group %s: Prot Switch Byte Failure - %s
vendor_explanation: This message is posted by the local network element if a Protection Switch Byte Failure is detected. A Protection Switch Byte Failure is detected when the Protection Switch Byte defect count exceeds a threshold. A Protection Switch Byte Defect is detected when one of the following happens: 1) The remote APS request is not one of the supported requests. 2) The remote APS request channel number is invalid. For 1+1 APS, the channel number must be 0 or 1. 3) Operation is bidirectional and neither local nor remote network element is sending a REVERSE-REQUEST, and the remote APS request is of lower priority than the local APS request. 4) Operation is bidirectional and the sequence number in the remote APS REVERSE-REQUEST does not match the sequence number of the most recent APS request sent by the local network element. This error is posted if a) the APS request is somehow corrupted, or b) there is a bug in the APS software itself or c) if the APS communication between two network elements is broken, e.g. local network element can send and receive, whereas the remote network element can send but not receive.
